_comment: Voice-over, one entry per video segment. {placeholders} are filled from docs/slides/deck_data.json.
title: Table for Two. Two robot arms set a dinner table from a single sentence, planned and driven on Intel OpenVINO.
plan: A small language model, running locally on OpenVINO, turns the instruction into a step-by-step plan. Before the robot moves, every plan is checked: the planner simulates what each hand is holding, so the arms never pour without the bottle.
demo: Now the learned policy takes over. It sees two camera views and its own joint positions, and outputs joint targets ten times a second. It opens the drawer, sets the spoon, hands the fork from the left arm to the right, and puts the plate on the placemat. Then one arm holds the mug while the other pours. On this scene, the learned policy completes every stage on its own.
grid: Robustness matters. Across ten held-out scenes we change object positions, masses, friction, lighting and the colour of the table. The scripted pipeline that generated our training data sets the full table in all ten.
results: On the same ten scenes, the learned policy alone completes the whole task in {policy_full_task}, and in {hybrid_full_task} when a script finishes the stages it times out on. Its weak spots are precise spoon placement and finishing the pour, and we report them as they are.
latency: On Intel hardware, NNCF INT8 quantisation runs the policy in {int8_cpu_ms} milliseconds on the CPU, {int8_speedup_words} faster than full precision.
closing: Grasps are constraint assisted, and stages finished by a script are never counted as policy wins. Everything you have seen is reproducible from our repository. Thank you.
